title: Keep a paper copy of your plan
summary: Phones run out of battery. Write down your emergency contacts and meeting places, and keep a copy where you can reach it.
body:
An app is only useful while your phone has power. In a long outage or an evacuation, a sheet of paper still works.

FEMA's Ready.gov recommends making a family emergency communication plan and writing it down. Put these on paper:
- Phone numbers for family members and an out-of-town contact
- Where to meet if you cannot get home, near home and out of the neighborhood
- Numbers for work, school or child care, and your doctors
- Your home address, so anyone can give it to a dispatcher

Give everyone in the household a copy, and keep one in your emergency kit, your car and your wallet or bag. Look it over every six months and update anything that has changed.

Ready.gov has a fillable plan template: https://www.ready.gov/plan
